skill.name: mobile-games
skill.description: Apply mobile game development principles for touch controls, responsive screens, performance, battery use, app stores, and monetization.
skill.summary: Design mobile games around platform constraints, player input, device performance, and store requirements.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives caused by harmless mobile development guidance. No system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or other malicious intent appears in the reviewed skill.

finding_verdicts.reason: The cited line advises avoiding precise timing requirements for touch input. It contains no system discovery command, data collection, or reconnaissance instruction.
The cited line is only an Android Google Play section heading. It contains no instruction to inspect a device, operating system, network, or credentials.

content.value_statement: Mobile games must balance touch usability, device limits, store rules, and business goals. This skill provides practical principles for making those decisions.
actual_capabilities: Recommends touch target sizes, feedback, gestures, and orientation support.
Defines performance responses for warm, hot, and critically hot devices.
Suggests frame rate, pause behavior, network use, and OLED battery optimizations.
Summarizes key iOS App Store and Google Play requirements.
Compares premium, in-app purchase, advertising, and subscription models.
Identifies mobile design anti-patterns and practical alternatives.
limitations: It provides principles, not engine-specific implementation code.
Store requirements can change and require current platform documentation.
Performance recommendations require testing on representative physical devices.
It does not replace privacy, legal, accessibility, or monetization compliance review.

use_cases.title: Plan a Mobile Control Scheme
use_cases.description: Review touch targets, gestures, screen occlusion, orientation, and feedback before implementation.

use_cases.title: Set Device Performance Targets
use_cases.description: Define frame rate, thermal throttling, pause behavior, and battery goals for a mobile build.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Store Release
use_cases.description: Create a checklist covering platform requirements, screenshots, privacy labels, packaging, and monetization choices.

prompt_templates.title: Review Touch Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my mobile game controls for touch usability, target size, feedback, screen occlusion, and orientation support.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has an early control concept.

prompt_templates.title: Create Performance Targets
prompt_templates.prompt: Create performance, thermal, battery, pause, and network targets for my [genre] game on [supported devices].
prompt_templates.scenario: A team is defining technical requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Release Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Build separate iOS and Android release checklists for my game, including store assets, privacy, account deletion, API level, and packaging.
prompt_templates.scenario: A producer is preparing store submission.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a Mobile Game Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this mobile game plan across controls, responsiveness, thermals, battery, interruptions, stores, monetization, and likely anti-patterns: [plan].
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced team needs a structured design review.

output_examples.input: Review a portrait puzzle game with small tiles and time-sensitive swipes.
output: Increase interactive areas to at least 44 by 44 points.
Add immediate visual feedback for every swipe and selection.
Reduce precision and timing demands where mistakes block progress.
Test whether fingers hide important puzzle information.

output_examples.input: Suggest thermal responses for an action game targeting 60 frames per second.
output: When warm, reduce visual quality before changing gameplay.
When hot, lower the frame rate and expensive effects.
At critical temperature, pause nonessential effects and protect stability.
Measure each response on representative physical devices.

output_examples.input: Outline store preparation for a game with player accounts.
output: Prepare privacy labels and screenshots for required iOS device sizes.
Provide account deletion because the game supports account creation.
Target the current required Android API level.
Confirm 64-bit support and prepare an Android App Bundle.

best_practices: Test touch controls and performance on representative physical devices.
Define thermal and battery responses before final optimization.
Verify current store requirements shortly before every release.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse desktop controls without redesigning them for touch.
Do not ignore battery drain, thermal limits, or background interruptions.
Do not require continuous network access when caching and synchronization are sufficient.

faq.question: Which mobile platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers general mobile constraints plus selected iOS App Store and Google Play requirements.

faq.question: Does it provide Unity or Unreal code?
faq.answer: No. It provides platform and design principles that can guide implementation in any engine.

faq.question: What touch target size does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends a minimum touch target of 44 by 44 points.

faq.question: Does it help with battery and thermal performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends frame rate, sleep, network, visual quality, and thermal response strategies.

faq.question: Can it guarantee app store approval?
faq.answer: No. Store policies change, so teams must verify current official requirements before submission.

faq.question: Does it recommend a monetization model?
faq.answer: It compares common models and their typical uses, but the final choice depends on the game and audience.
